title: Mary Nelson's mission to feed kids carries on with or without the district - NewsBreak
text: SYRACUSE, N.Y. (WSYR-TV)— For years, Mary Nelson’s Youth Center has become a lifeline for children, especially those on Syracuse’s southside, offering kids free meals and a safe and caring environment. But this summer, a broken air conditioner and a surprise state inspection changed everything for her summer food program. The Mary Nelson Youth Center partnered with the Syracuse City School District as one of the locations of its feeding program, which began on July 7. The program offers breakfast at 9:00 a.m. and lunch at 11:00 a.m. But just a week in, when the center’s A/C broke, raising the heat inside the youth center, Mary said she made a choice: serve both meals at one, let the kids take it home, and keep them out of the center’s heat. “Some kids came in the door and I said, listen, we’re going to do something different today, and I gotta do something different because I don’t want you guys coming in here to heat today, it is so hot,” said Mary Nelson, President & CEO for The Mary Nelson Youth Center. That change to adapt to the situation didn’t follow state guidelines. A surprise auditor, who came that day, flagged it as a violation. Soon after, the district visited her center and explained the changes needed to stay in the program. Rather than complying with the district, she asked them to stop bringing meals and continues to feed the children her way. Even without the district’s food, she said her mission is still the same. “These children mean so much to me…so much to me, and their safety and their health comes first,” said the President & CEO of the Southside Youth Center. Yet thanks to a donation from Hummingbird Heating & Cooling, a new air conditioning system is being installed at the center. “They surprised me,” Nelson said. “They’re getting me two furnaces and an air conditioner. That’s the power of God—and the love this community has for our babies.” In a statement regarding the surprise visits made to four locations of the district’s community meal sites, the Syracuse City School District said, “As part of the corrective action, the NYSED agreed upon positioning one of SCSD’s seasoned food service staff members to correct the findings from their audit. The district provided the corrective action information to Ms. Mary Nelson regarding the start time/dates and roles and responsibilities of our food service staff member that would be assigned to her site moving forward. Unfortunately, she declined to have anyone on location and preferred not to use our food. However, if at any point Ms. Nelson would like to reinstitute with our staff present, we would be more than willing to do so and appreciate the partnership she has provided.” For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WSYR.
